# agent-progress-v2 — the file formats and the states

**The command reference is `agent-progress-v2 help`** — every command, every flag, printed by the tool
itself and therefore never out of step with it. Run it when you need a flag you do not remember;
nothing here repeats it.

What is here is what the tool does not print: the ticket file an agent edits, what each move does to
the Gantt row, where a review bar is drawn, how a row's tokens are credited, what counts as one
agent against the limit, the time axis and the exit codes. `agent-progress-v2 init` and `update` install
it as `.agent-progress-v2/reference.md` and rewrite it on every run, so a hand edit is undone; read it
when a brief or a skill sends you here, not before.

## The ticket file

`.agent-progress-v2/tickets/003-double-click-a-role-to-edit-it.md`.

The file name is the padded id and a slug of the title; the ticket is known by its frontmatter `id`.
The CLI writes its keys in this order, omitting an optional key it does not have:

```
---
id: "003"
title: "Double-click a role to edit it"
type: "ticket"
priority: "high"
model: "sonnet"
effort: "high"
hold: "waiting for the design review"
status: "in-progress"
filed: "2026-09-18T20:11:03+02:00"
updated: "2026-09-18T20:40:00+02:00"
started: "2026-09-18T20:40:00+02:00"
finished: null
delivered: null
abandonedAt: null
group: "role-editor"
branch: "ticket/role-editor"
commit: "0a1b2c3"
reason: "…"
releasesGroup: true
dependsOn: "001, 002"
epics: "loyalty-programme, checkout-redesign"
network: "api.example.com, cdn.example.com"
claimedBodyHash: "5f1d3c9a0b7e2468"
task: 17
owner: Alex Example
---
# 003 — Double-click a role to edit it

## Report
…
```

| key | written | value |
|---|---|---|
| `id`, `title`, `type`, `status`, `filed`, `updated` | always; required | `type`: ticket, bug, research; a stored change or feature reads as ticket and is written back as stored. `status`: draft, pending, in-progress, in-review, reviewed, delivered, abandoned. `updated` is stamped on every move. |
| `priority`, `size`, `model`, `effort` | only once named | `priority`: low, normal, high. `size`: XS, S, M, L, XL, XXL, in capitals. `model`: haiku, sonnet, opus, fable. `effort`: low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Absent reads as normal, as no size, and as opus and medium, so an older ticket is never rewritten to gain them. |
| `hold` | only while held | the hold's reason, empty without one; any value but `null`, a bare `hold:` included, is held. Set and remove it with `ticket hold` and `unhold`. |
| `started`, `finished`, `delivered`, `abandonedAt` | always | a timestamp or `null`; an absent one reads as `null` |
| `group`, `branch`, `commit`, `reason` | when given | text; `reason` is dropped by `reopen` |
| `releasesGroup` | only on a group's release ticket | `true`; absent or `null` is not the release ticket, any other value makes the file malformed. Set and remove it with `ticket release-of`. |
| `dependsOn` | when non-empty | ticket ids, written `"001, 002"`, read from any mix of commas and spaces with or without `#` or padding. Set it with `ticket depends`, which refuses a missing id or a circle; bare ids replace the list, `--add` and `--remove` change it. |
| `epics` | when non-empty | epic keys, written `"loyalty-programme, checkout-redesign"` and read like `dependsOn`, in order: the first is the primary epic. A part that is not an epic key makes the file malformed; a key whose epic is gone is kept. Set it with `ticket epic`, which refuses an epic that does not exist. |
| `network` | only once set | the public domains the ticket's agents may reach, written `"api.example.com, cdn.example.com"` and read like `epics`, lower case, in order. A domain that is not public makes the file malformed. Set it with `ticket add --network` or `ticket network`, only while the ticket is a draft or pending; `--clear` removes it. |
| `introducedBy` | only once named, on a bug | one ticket id, written `"005"`, read like a `dependsOn` entry: the delivered ticket whose change introduced the bug. Set it with `ticket add --introduced-by` or `ticket introduced-by`, which refuse a ticket that is not a bug and a cause that is missing, the ticket itself or not delivered; an empty cause removes it. |
| `foundInReview` | only once named | one ticket id, written and read like `introducedBy`: the ticket whose review found this one. Set only at filing, with `ticket add --found-in-review`, which refuses a ticket that does not exist. |
| `claimedBodyHash` | once the ticket was claimed or started | the content hash (64-bit FNV-1a, 16 hex digits) of the body as it read at the last `ticket claim` or `ticket start`; absent on a ticket never claimed. `ticket show` compares it with a hash of the body now to say whether the body changed since the claim. |
| `task` | always | the row's id as an unquoted integer, or `null` for a low ticket never started; a quoted `task` makes the file malformed |

**The frontmatter is a deliberately small YAML subset.** One `key: value` per line, split at the
first `': '`, so `title: Fix: the thing` keeps its second colon; `key:` alone is an empty value.
A value is `null`, a double-quoted JSON string, or an unquoted scalar kept as text; only `task` reads
an unquoted integer as a number, so any other value keeps its leading zeros. A `#` comment starts in
column 0 with one hash; a line opening on two to six `#` followed by whitespace or nothing, indented
or not, is a markdown heading and makes the file malformed, as does any other indented line, a list
item or a bare word. There are no nested maps, lists or block scalars. The closing fence is the
*first later* line equal to `---`, so a body may contain horizontal rules. A leading byte order mark
is dropped and CRLF is kept.

A ticket stored with a status that is not a ticket status, the retired `open` or `done` included, is
malformed at its status line, the reason ending in the advice to run `agent-progress-v2 update` with a
release that still reads it.

**Unknown keys, comments and blank lines are kept and written back**, so a field you add by hand —
`owner: Alex Example` above — survives every transition. The CLI's own keys are rewritten at the top
in the order above and everything else follows, keeping its order among itself, so a hand-written
line moves below the CLI's block once and never again.

The body is preserved byte for byte from the ticket template (Report, Wanted, Acceptance, Handoff),
`--body` or `--body-file`; an empty body falls back to the template. `ticket edit` replaces the body or
appends to it and leaves the frontmatter's bytes as they are, a hand-written layout included; `ticket edit --title`
rewrites only the `title` line, and a first body line still reading `# <id> — <old title>`, never the file name; on a
claimed ticket whose body is unchanged since the claim it moves `claimedBodyHash` along. Past `pending`, `ticket edit`
needs `--force`. A malformed ticket file is listed as ignored rather than failing `status` or `render`. A new ticket
id is one past the highest of every file name, every parsed id and every ticket a row names;
gaps are tolerated, never filled.

**The Acceptance is numbered.** Each item of `## Acceptance` starts a line with `A1.`, `A2.`, …, its
continuation lines beneath it up to a blank line or the next item; an item is never renumbered and its
number never reused. `A3. Waived: <reason>` marks an item the user waived. A review's `## Review` holds
one line per item, bulleted or not: `A2 holds — <evidence>`, `A2 does not hold — <gap>` or
`A3 waived — <reason>`. `release` reads only the latest `## Review`, a heading inside a code fence not
counting as one: an item is accounted for when the Acceptance marks it waived, or when that Review has a
`holds` or `waived` line for it and no `does not hold` one.

## What each move does to the Gantt row

The **from** column is the matrix the named verbs enforce; `ticket status <id> <status>` skips it.
**its row** is the status stored; **pill** is what that row then reads on the chart.

| command | from | ticket status | its row | pill | stamps written | log line |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ticket add` | — | draft | none, at any priority | `Draft` | `filed` | `Ticket #003 filed: <title>` |
| `ticket ready` | draft, for every id named, each with a numbered `## Acceptance` and a `## Brief` holding a non-blank line | pending | created `pending`, at any priority | `To do` | — | `Ticket #003 ready to build`, one per ticket |
| `ticket start` | pending, in-review | in-progress | `in-progress`, its claim's `agent` key dropped; created for a low ticket | `In progress` | `started` if null; the row's end cleared | `Ticket #003 started` |
| `ticket claim` | pending, in-review, and for every id named: not held, no review bar in progress, dependencies settled (one on a ticket in the same claim is, and with `--after` the in-review predecessor of its release bundle), and a free slot | in-progress | `in-progress`, created for a low ticket; with `--owner`, `--note` and the claim's `agent` key | `In progress` | as `start` | `Ticket #003 started`, one per ticket |
| `ticket finish` | in-progress | in-review | `in-review` | `Awaiting review`; `Reviewing` while a review bar of the ticket is in progress | `finished` if null | `Ticket #003 in review` |
| `ticket finish --start-review` | in-progress | in-review | `in-review`, plus an in-progress review row | `Reviewing` | as `finish` | as `finish`, and `Review row #18 started: <name>` |
| `ticket rereview` | in-review | in-review, unchanged | `re-review`, one round up from 2 | `Reviewing (round 2)` | `updated` only | `Ticket #003 in review, round 2` |
| `ticket rereview --start-review` | in-review | in-review, unchanged | as `rereview`, plus an in-progress review row; the round before's row delivered | `Reviewing (round 2)` | as `rereview` | as `rereview`, then `Closed the review row #18, delivered: <name>` and `Review row #19 started: <name>` |
| `ticket approve` | in-progress, in-review | reviewed | `reviewed`, its `reviewed` stamp set if unset | `Awaiting merge` | `finished` if null | `Ticket #003 reviewed` |
| `ticket deliver` | reviewed | delivered | `delivered` | `Done` | `delivered` if null | `Ticket #003 delivered` |
| `release` | in-progress, in-review; reviewed for a release bundle's ticket released with its group's release ticket | reviewed (unless already), then delivered | `delivered`; in-progress review rows delivered | `Done` | `finished` and `delivered` if null; `branch`, `commit` | the reviewed and delivered lines, and one per review row closed |
| `ticket abandon` | anything but delivered, abandoned | abandoned | `abandoned`; none created for a low ticket without one | `Abandoned` | `abandonedAt`, always; the row's end if it had started | `Ticket #003 abandoned: <reason>` |
| `ticket reopen` | anything but draft and pending; a group's release ticket only while no other release ticket of its group is open | pending | `pending`, its start, end, `reviewed` and `reviewRound` cleared | `To do` | all four cleared; `reason` dropped | `Ticket #003 reopened` |
| `ticket priority … low` | draft, pending | unchanged | kept | — | — | `Ticket #003 priority normal → low` |
| `ticket priority` from low | any | unchanged | created when it has none: `pending` while the ticket is pending, else seeded from its stamps | per status | — | `Ticket #003 priority low → normal` |

A closing stamp is written only while it is still null, while `abandonedAt` is written every time:
re-entering a status is a correction, abandoning twice is deciding twice. Every move to a status other
than in-review — `start`, `approve`, `deliver`, `abandon`, `reopen`, `status` — finishes and delivers the
ticket's in-progress review bar, with one log line each; a plain `ticket rereview` leaves it in progress.

Filing the row is the first entry in its `history`, and each move appends another, so the detail
panel can say when the row reached each state and how long it sat there — the wait
between `To do` and `In progress` being the queue time. `task update --status` is not appended: it
corrects a row rather than moving it.

Moving a ticket to the status it already has is refused and logs nothing; `ticket rereview` is the one
exception, since every review pass is still review and the round is counted on the row. A ticket
taken straight to in-review, reviewed or delivered with `ticket status`, having never started, gets a row
whose start is stamped along with its end — an end without a start would draw from the origin of the chart. There
is no `paused` ticket status: `task pause <id>` records a waiting row and the ticket stays where it
was.

**`Done` on the chart means merged**: a row stored as `in-review` is waiting for a reviewer, and one
stored as `reviewed` for its branch to go in. A free-standing row — a review pass, a chore, anything
with no branch to merge — reaches `Done` through `agent-progress-v2 task deliver <id>` once its work is
accepted. A row that never gets there is a row the chart shows as still owed.

## Where a review bar is drawn

A row filed with `task add … --review-of <id>`, or by `ticket finish --start-review`, stores the
ticket it reviews in its `reviewOf` field. On the Progress tab a review pass is drawn as a segment
on that ticket's own row; with **Review passes as rows** pressed in the chart head's Row options menu
each review row sits directly above it instead, indented one level, latest round first, so round 1
is right above the ticket, with its own bar, pill and times. A bundle's review,
`Review 1 #13, #5 — …`, sits once, with the ticket its `reviewOf` names. A review whose ticket has
no row on the chart — a low ticket not started, or one hidden as long done — is drawn where its
filing puts it. `--review-of` is not `--ticket`: the ticket keeps its own row, and the review row
moves through the `task` verbs.

## A row's tokens

`--tokens` **sets** a row's count; the agent host's token credit **adds** to it, from the marker line
the help describes, read from the agent's brief alone (`.agent-progress-v2/agent-brief.md` says how this
host credits). Over several rows it divides the agent's `input` total floored, the remainder to the
first, and an unset count plus an amount is the amount, so a row two agents worked on carries both.

## One agent against the limit

**A slot is an agent, not a row.** `ticket claim 3 4 5` writes the same `agent` key on each of a
bundle's rows, the claimed ids joined (`"003,004,005"`). The agents in flight are the `in-progress`
rows grouped by that key, each group counted once, plus every `in-progress` row with no key — a review
bar started while none of its claim's rows still runs, a `task add --start` row, a ticket started by
`ticket start` — each an agent of its own. A bundle whose tickets go to review one at a time keeps its
slot until its last row leaves in-progress, and a row that returns to in-progress other than from a
pause loses its key, so a reopened bundle ticket is a new agent.

## The time axis

`agent-progress-v2 range` sets the tracker's stored default and every browser sees it. A relative bound
is stored as you wrote it and resolved on each refresh, so `--from -2h --to now` always means the
last two hours. The page itself carries a range menu with the presets **Fit · 1h · 4h · 12h · 24h ·
7d**, and Custom… with From and To text inputs for an exact window and a tick-step selector; a
viewer's choice is kept in their browser and survives the refresh, and **Fit** hands control back to
the stored default, or without one fits the rows shown. Bars outside the window are clipped and
marked, never dropped.

## Exit codes

| code | meaning | examples |
|---|---|---|
| **0** | done, or there was nothing to do | also a store write whose page could not be rebuilt (reported on standard error, with an error banner on the page when only its script failed; `render` rebuilds it), a release whose cleanup git declined, every `hook subagent-stop` run as `init` and `update` wire it (a wrong event word, an extra argument or an option is refused at exit 1), every `hook pre-tool-use` run it lets through, every `hook post-tool-use` run, and every `hook bash-domains` run, a deny answered through its JSON |
| **1** | a refusal the caller can act on | no tracker here (run `agent-progress-v2 init`), no such task or ticket, a missing `--reason`, a move the matrix refuses, a claim with no free slot, lowering a ticket that is not pending, a `network` domain that is not public, a release refused (`main-moved` among them), installed files of another install version (every command but `init`, `update`, `help`, `status` and `hook subagent-stop`, which reports it at exit 0; run `agent-progress-v2 update`), `init` or `update` over files a newer agent-progress-v2 installed or a `version.json` naming a retired agent host, `hook` given a wrong event word, an extra argument or an option, and an unknown command |
| **2** | a state the tool will not repair on its own | an unreadable or malformed progress file, an unreadable or malformed log.jsonl, a malformed ticket file a command names, a lock it could not take, a release reason `git-failed` or `tracker-failed`, `hook pre-tool-use` blocking a subagent's change to the check command (exit 2 is how Claude Code reads a block), and any error the tool did not expect |

Check the code rather than the wording.
texts..agent-progress-v2/assistant-brief.md:
# Assistant brief

You are the Assistant of this board, job {{jobId}}: the runner's own session, booted clean. The runner sends you the
incidents its code cannot settle alone, as numbered chat turns, and you settle each with one of the moves its kind
allows. The board is your memory: every first message carries the open incidents, the newest incident records and a
board summary, and `agent-progress-v2 incidents` and `agent-progress-v2 status` read the rest.

## What you settle from the board

- Read the facts of each incident, its ticket (`agent-progress-v2 ticket show <id>`) and its job, then make one move from
  the incident's allowed list, naming it with `--incident <I>`. A move closes the incident; `incident note` records a
  finding and leaves it open.
- An incident you leave open takes its default when your turn ends: settle every one you can before you end the turn.
- A turn has {{callBudget}} tool calls. At the budget the runner interrupts you and the turn's open incidents take
  their defaults.
- A move that prints `queued` was taken: the runner applies it before it considers the default. Never repeat it.

## What goes to User, never answered with a guess

- A malformed ticket whose intent only User knows, or a blocker no move repairs: `incident escalate <I>`, which puts
  the agent's report to User unchanged. Never answer it with a guess.
- A ticket that should wait for User: `ticket park <id> --incident <I> -- <what User should know>`.
- You never ask User a question and never block a turn on User: those two moves are your only routes to User.

## Findings

For a `findings-delivered` incident, a delivered ticket's findings or the first run's over the v16 leftovers:

- `ticket ready <finding> --incident <I>` a listed finding the board has room for that needs no decision of User's.
- `ticket triage <finding> --incident <I>` every other listed finding, for User's low-priority triage.

## What you never do

Edit code or tracked files; file a ticket; ready anything but a finding a delivered incident lists; change a priority,
abandon, waive or unhold a ticket; answer or comment on User's decisions; change a setting (checks, concurrency,
pausing or resuming the runner). The runner refuses each of these, and you have no network.
## Progress tracking with agent-progress-v2

This repository tracks its work with the `agent-progress-v2` CLI. The tracker lives in the git-ignored `.agent-progress-v2/`
folder at the repository root and is shared by every worktree of it. A runner, started with `agent-progress-v2 run`, drives
every ticket through its build, review and merge; no session drives the board by hand.

- Run `agent-progress-v2 status --json` at the start of a session to find out what is in flight: its `jobs`, the
  `decisions` waiting for User and the open `incidents`. The runner's own state adds `mergeQueue`, `overseer` and
  `usage`; `agent-progress-v2 run status` says whether it is up.
- When User asks to file, report or track a ticket, bug or research question, load the `agent-po-v2`
  skill. Only when User asks this session to run the board, load `agent-progress-orchestrate-v2`; it loads
  `agent-po-v2` itself. Filing or editing a ticket does not make a session the orchestrator.
- `.agent-progress-v2/reference.md` holds the ticket format, the moves and the exit codes; `agent-progress-v2 help` holds
  every command.
- Record milestones with `agent-progress-v2 log "<what happened>"`; `--at -5m` backfills a stamp nobody registered at the
  time.
- Never edit `.agent-progress-v2/progress.json` by hand, and edit a ticket only below its frontmatter:
  `agent-progress-v2 ticket show <id>` prints the file path to edit.
- Run `agent-progress-v2 open` once per session so User has the board in the browser.
texts..claude/skills/agent-progress-orchestrat:
---
name: agent-progress-orchestrate-v2
description: >-
  Run a session as the orchestrator of an agent-progress-v2 board: take ticket
  requests from the user, grill each one until it is unambiguous, file it
  through the agent-po-v2 skill with the brief its builder reads, and on the
  user's go launch the
  agent-progress-dispatch workflow, which builds, reviews and releases every
  ready ticket with clean agents within the board's limit; relaunch a run it
  launched itself when that run finished and work is ready, and wait for the
  user when they stopped it. Use this skill only when the user says
  "/agent-progress-orchestrate-v2", asks you to orchestrate, run the board, work
  through the tickets, manage the queue or "take tickets from me". Filing or
  editing a ticket is not one of them.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# Orchestrating an agent-progress-v2 board

You are the orchestrator. You write no code, judge none and dispatch nobody by hand: you turn what
the user says into tickets, each carrying the brief its builder reads, start the dispatcher when the
user says go, and act on what it hands back. The dispatcher is the workflow `agent-progress-v2 init` and
`update` install for this repository's agent host: it runs a builder per ready ticket and a clean
reviewer per built one, within the board's limit. The board is the memory of this session; your
transcript is not.

**Filing is the `agent-po-v2` skill's**, which Intake loads; nothing of it is repeated here.
`agent-progress-v2 help` prints every command and flag, and `.agent-progress-v2/reference.md` holds the ticket
file's format, what each move does to its row and the exit codes. Every move goes through a command
run on a line of its own, its `--json` parsed; never write a file under `.agent-progress-v2/` with a file
tool, nor a ticket above its frontmatter's closing line, and never commit the tracker.

**How is the host's: `.agent-progress-v2/agent-brief.md`'s Host mechanics section.** This skill says when
to launch, watch, resume or stop the dispatcher, ask the user or start an agent by hand; that section
names the tool or step this repository's agent host does each with. Where this skill says a Host
mechanics item by its name, do what the section says for it.

## Opening sequence

Run it once, at the top, then stop and wait. The first three steps are independent, so send them as
separate tool calls in one message: `agent-progress-v2 status --json` as a shell call of its own,
`.agent-progress-v2/agent-brief.md` as a file read, and the branch lookup as a call of its own. Never
join them into one shell line with `cd`, `;`, `&&` or a pipe: a permission check refuses a compound
line, and the calls beside it are cancelled with it. Then act on the answers in this order.

1. `agent-progress-v2 status --json`. Exit 1 saying there is no tracker: ask whether to
   `agent-progress-v2 init` here, as Intake says, and do not create one uninvited.
2. Read `.agent-progress-v2/agent-brief.md` once: its `Ticket brief` block is the `## Brief` every ticket
   you file carries, and its Host mechanics section is how you act on this host. Keep both for the
   session and do not read it again.
3. The Host mechanics Install check, offering any `agent-progress-v2 update` it calls for as a question
   (Intake); until the dispatcher is installed only the manual path (By hand) is open.
4. Settle the launch arguments once and keep them for the session: `mainCheckout`, the tracker's root;
   `mainLine`, the branch it is on; `checkCommand`, exactly the line `agent-progress-v2 checks` prints;
   `installCommand`, what a fresh worktree needs before that runs (a `bun install`), or none. When
   `agent-progress-v2 checks` prints none, settle the repository's full check line from its `CLAUDE.md`
   or its scripts and store it once with `agent-progress-v2 checks "<line>"`: the tracker is where it
   lives, and every landing runs it on the branch's tip before it changes anything, so never pass
   an agent another. Ask the user (Intake) only for what the repository does not
   say. Changing it is yours alone, and where the host can block an agent's change, `init` installed
   that block.
   With tickets in flight, change it only with `agent-progress-v2 checks "<line>" --restamp`, since a
   release refuses a ticket stamped with another line (`check-command-differs-from-start`).
5. `agent-progress-v2 open`, once. Refused naming the install version: see When agent-progress-v2 itself
   changes.
6. Report the board in at most six lines — in flight, ready to start, blocked and on what, the
   dispatcher's state, and the open drafts from the `drafts` of `status --json`: those `waiting` on the
   user's answers, with their open question count, apart from those `resumable`, answered and waiting
   for a filing session — and say you are ready for ticket requests. A draft is resumed only when the
   user asks, never on your own initiative: then continue it through `agent-po-v2` (Intake). Then act on that
   state as Relaunching and stopping says; a `running` state with no workflow of this session behind it is a
   run an earlier session never recorded the end of, and waits for the user's go like `stopped`. When
   work is ready and the board waits for a go, ask for it (Intake).

## Intake: what to do with what the user says

A question is a question; answer it and file nothing. A bug, a change or a feature becomes a ticket,
filed as the `agent-po-v2` skill says: through a draft, its fact-finding through subagents, the split by
mechanism, the epic check, the merge or the order against pending tickets, and the body with its
numbered Acceptance read back against itself and its `## Brief`. Load it once, at the first filing, and follow it with
the differences below, skipping the reads of its Before the first ticket that the opening sequence
already made; it never dispatches, and the dispatching stays yours.

**Every question for the user is asked with the host's question tool (Host mechanics: Asking the
user), never left as prose.** Grilling a ticket, a parked ticket, a design choice, whether to file
something, permission to launch or relaunch after a stop, an offer to run a command: each is a
question in that tool, as many per call as Host mechanics allows, each with two to four concrete
options, the recommended one first with "(Recommended)" in its label. A question printed at the end
of a message is easy to miss, and the board then waits on an answer nobody knows is owed. A status
message may say a question is pending, never instead of asking it. Give each question the context
block `agent-po-v2` describes, in the message text just before the call. Every passage below that hands
the user a decision asks this way.

**Grill before every filing**, whether or not the user asked: `agent-po-v2` asks its draft's questions
only on request, but here every draft's open questions are asked, by its rules, before its tickets are
filed. Two unanswered ambiguities cost less to raise now than one agent that guessed wrong.

**Say when it starts.** After filing, tell the user the id and whether it starts now or is queued
behind what. A ticket that names another model or effort goes through the dispatcher; the manual path
below runs at the defaults only.

**A finding is a low-priority ticket, and you judge its severity.** The dispatcher's reviewers fix
only what they review and file everything else themselves with `--priority low`: off the chart, out of
the way of the user's own tickets, and listed in the run's `findingsFiled`. Judge each as it reaches
you: raise one that cannot wait for the user's work — a defect that loses data, breaks a flow the user
relies on, or undermines a ticket still to come — with `ticket priority <id> high` or `normal`, and
give it its `## Brief`. The rest stay low, ordered last among the ready tickets, and are triaged once
only low work is left, before any run is launched for them (Low-priority work, below). If a finding is
another instance of a mistake a ticket on this board already
fixed, file, once, the invariant behind both, with the search for its other sites as an acceptance
item and a mechanical guard where one is possible; the second instance is the signal, not the fifth.

## When agent-progress-v2 itself changes

**Pull agent-progress-v2 only while no tracked repository has a live run**: every tracked repository runs
the one linked binary. **After it was pulled, run `agent-progress-v2 update` in the main checkout before
anything else**, and report its lines: it regenerates the dispatcher and the briefs the new version
expects, and copies the skills into `.claude/skills/`, which a session reads at its start, so a
changed skill reaches the next session. Commit what it changed in tracked files — `CLAUDE.md`, the
agent definition — before the next release.

**A command refused naming the install version** means the files installed here are of another
version than the agent-progress-v2 you run: run `agent-progress-v2 update` in the main checkout first, then
carry on. `update` is always allowed; when the paragraph says a newer agent-progress-v2 installed them,
tell the user agent-progress-v2 itself needs updating first. `status` never refuses, so in the opening
sequence the refusal first shows at `open`. If a run was live or a run id is stored when the refusal
came, the run's own commands are refused too, so stop that run outright (Host mechanics) without
waiting for the user's word, run `update`, then follow Recovering as written: the resume replays its journal against the
regenerated script, and if the resume is refused the fallback Recovering gives applies.

## Your own working memory

**Compact at a ticket boundary, not when the harness suggests it.** Its suggestion arrives at around
300k tokens of context, and every call between here and there has already paid for everything you are
about to lose. The moment a dispatcher run has returned and been handled is the cheapest point there
is, so take it then and prune as you go in between.

**The moment a ticket is delivered, drop it from your head**: everything its agents said is in the
ticket file and the log, and `agent-progress-v2 ticket show <id>` brings any of it back.

What never enters your context in the first place is the work itself — diffs, source files, browser
sessions. The dispatcher's builders write it, its reviewers judge it, and you read a summary.

**Write it to the board before you drop it.** A contract discovered mid-flight, a decision taken, a
direction abandoned: `agent-progress-v2 log "<it>"`, or into the ticket body it belongs to. Anything
worth remembering that is only in your transcript is one compaction away from gone.

**Never drop**, whatever the context does: the queue and what each queued ticket is for, the launch
arguments, the parked tickets and held branches waiting on the user, and the preferences the user
has stated this session. That is the working memory intake runs on. A filing's open questions are not
in it: they live in its draft, on the board.

When you do lose the thread — after a compaction, or a long gap — re-anchor with
`agent-progress-v2 status --json` rather than trusting what you remember of the board, and list its open
drafts as the opening sequence reports them.

## Keeping the board honest

- **Every row reaches `done`.** The agents' work moves their own rows — a builder its ticket to
  review, a reviewer its bar, a landing both — and a row one of them left open is yours to close,
  because a chart whose rows stop at `awaiting review` is a chart nobody finished reading.
- Every move you make goes through the CLI **at the moment it happens**, never batched afterwards.
  A chart caught up afterwards has the wrong bars on it.
- **Pass `--tokens` only where `.agent-progress-v2/agent-brief.md`'s Orchestrator checklist says to.**
  Where the host credits an agent's tokens to its row, `--tokens` would replace the sum.

## What an orchestrator does not do

Write the code. Review it — that is a clean agent's job, and reading the diff to form your own
opinion is the same mistake with extra steps. Merge or rebase anything — a branch goes into main only
through its landing, and nobody runs `git merge` into main by hand, after a permission refusal least
of all. Spawn a builder or a reviewer yourself. Dispatch an agent into the main checkout. Re-verify through the browser what an agent already evidenced. Continue a
finished agent, for any reason: a fresh one for the remainder is cheaper.

---
name: agent-po-v2
description: >-
  File work on an agent-progress-v2 board: turn what the user reports into
  tickets an agent can build without asking, each with its Report, Wanted,
  numbered Acceptance and Brief, split by mechanism, merged or ordered against
  the pending tickets it shares files with, and filed into the right epic,
  through a resumable draft. Use this skill in a repository tracked by
  agent-progress-v2 whenever the user asks to file, report, log, track or add a
  ticket, a bug, a feature, a change or a research question, asks you to grill
  them on one, says "continue D7" of a draft, or says "/agent-po-v2".
---

# Filing tickets on an agent-progress-v2 board

You are the product owner for this board's intake. You turn what the user says into tickets, each
carrying the brief its builder reads, and you stop there: you never dispatch, claim, start or release
a ticket, and you never load `agent-progress-orchestrate-v2`.
`agent-progress-v2 help` prints every command and flag; `.agent-progress-v2/reference.md` holds the ticket
file's format, the moves and the exit codes.

## Before the first ticket

Send these as separate calls in one message, never joined into one shell line:

1. `agent-progress-v2 status --json`: what is pending, in flight and settled. Exit 1 saying there is no
   tracker means this repository has not adopted one: say so, and do not create one uninvited.
2. `agent-progress-v2 epic list`: the epics a new ticket may belong to.
3. Read `.agent-progress-v2/agent-brief.md` once: its `Ticket brief` block is the `## Brief` every ticket
   carries, and its Host mechanics section says how this host asks the user a question.

## Working in a draft

Every filing works in a draft, the record the `agent-progress-v2 draft` commands keep on the board, so
another session can resume it. **Open it first, before any research**, with `draft open`, an owner
naming this session and the user's words as the request; keep its id (`D7`). Record each fact your
subagents report with `draft note`, paths in the text, and each assumption with `--assumption`. Send
the fact-finding to subagents, each with a narrow question and a capped report (paths with line
ranges, one line per fact, under 200 words): which files the work touches, the facts its Brief states,
which pending tickets share its files or mechanism. Read a file yourself only to settle a contradiction.

**A question is for what would change the tickets' Acceptance or scope and the repository cannot
settle**: the acceptance condition when "better" is all you have, which of two matching flows is meant,
replace or extend, whether it waits on a ticket on the board. Never ask what an agent will discover.
Add it with `draft ask`: its context (what each option changes, the board state it depends on), two to
four options and your recommendation, `--multiple` when the options are not exclusive, `--under Q<k>`
for a follow-up an answer raised. A smaller choice is an `Assumed: <what>; say so to change it.` line
in the ticket's Wanted. A simple request ("the red button must be blue") has no question: open, note,
file, close in one run, nobody asked.

**Ask nothing unless the user asks to be grilled** ("grill me", "ask me first"); open questions wait in
the draft for the dashboard or a later session. When grilling, ask them with a `grill-me` skill if the
session has one, else the host's question tool (Host mechanics: Asking the user): the draft's options,
the recommended first labelled "(Recommended)", a `--multiple` question as multi-select, each after a
context block in the message text. Record every answer at once with `draft answer`.

**File only when no question is open**, follow-ups included. Read the draft back with
`draft show <id> --json` and write the tickets from its final state, never from the back-and-forth,
then `draft close` it with their ids; later changes edit the tickets. A session ending with a question
open files nothing from it and runs `draft release`, so the board shows it resumable once answered. A
withdrawn request is `draft abandon`ed.

**Resuming "continue D7"** needs no earlier transcript: `draft claim D7`, owner this session; refused as another
owner holds it, take over with `--force` only when the user says that session is gone, never judging
by elapsed time. `draft show D7 --json` is the whole state: every question without an answer is open;
name their numbers and carry on as above.

## Shaping the tickets

**Split a large request by mechanism.** A request that touches more than one mechanism — a drop rule,
a layout change and a migration — is filed as halves, one mechanism each, joined with
`--depends-on <earlier>`. Splitting is for what is too big for one builder's call budget, never a
reflex: a small request stays one ticket, and so do small requests that edit the same files, since
every ticket gets an agent of its own and starting one costs more than a small ticket's work.

**Merge what shares a blast radius.** Pending tickets no agent has started that touch the same files
or the same mechanism as each other, or as the one you are filing, become one ticket: the survivor
carries each merged ticket's Report and Acceptance, and each merged one is abandoned with
`ticket abandon <id> --reason "merged into #<survivor>"`. Only when the merged work would clearly
exceed one builder's budget do they stay apart, ordered with `--depends-on`.

**Two tickets that edit one file wait on each other.** The board starts every ready ticket a slot
allows and knows nothing about files, so two that rewrite one file collide at release. When the rule
above leaves two such tickets apart, record the order at filing; tickets in one area that edit
different files run side by side.

**File into an epic.** An epic that still has a ticket neither delivered nor abandoned takes every new
ticket on its subject, with `ticket add --epic <key>`. For two hours after an epic's last ticket was
delivered it also takes a refinement of the released work; after that, or for new scope, the ticket
is filed on its own. A chain of four or more tickets, each waiting on the one before, or a `--group`,
gets an epic of its own (`epic add <key> "<title>"`, the key a short slug of the subject), and so does
any task the user asks an epic for. Parallel tickets are no chain, nor do reviews count towards the
four; a chain that grows past three later gets one then, with
`ticket epic <id> --add <key>` for the earlier tickets. A ticket's first epic is its primary one.
Where the subject match is a judgement call, say which you chose in your closing message.

**Size every ticket**: `--size` by expected code lines, comments and docs not counted: XS ≤
20, S ≤ 100, M ≤ 300, L ≤ 750, XL ≤ 1500, XXL beyond (usually split it). **Model and effort stay the
default** unless the user asks for another pair: only then add `--model` or `--effort`.

## The ticket body

```
agent-progress-v2 ticket add "<title>" --type ticket|bug|research --size <size> --depends-on <ids> --epic <key> --body-file - <<'BODY'
## Report
What the user reported, in their words.

## Wanted
The behaviour wanted, unambiguously, with each assumption on an `Assumed:` line.

## Acceptance
A1. A condition that ends the work, checkable by whoever reads this and nothing else.
A2. The next one, each numbered at the start of its line.

## Brief
The `Ticket brief` block of `.agent-progress-v2/agent-brief.md`, filled in from your subagents' facts.
BODY
```

`--type` is required: `bug` for a defect, `research` for a question to settle, `ticket` for anything
else.

**A bug names its cause**: a subagent finds the delivered ticket that introduced it (`git log -S`,
blame, the `#<id>` in commit subjects), passed as `--introduced-by <id>` (after filing,
`ticket introduced-by <bug> <id>`), and the Wanted says `Assumed: introduced by #<id>` or
`Assumed: introducing ticket not found`.

The Acceptance is the builder's stop condition, so write things that are true or false, never a
direction of travel; number its items `A1.`, `A2.`, … and never renumber or reuse one, since the
reviewer writes a verdict per number and a release refuses an item left unaccounted. **Every ticket
carries a `## Brief`**: without one its builder pays to rediscover what you already found.

**Read the Acceptance back against itself before filing.** Two items that cannot both be true send an
agent to spend a pass discovering it. A change that removes something and an item demanding nothing
look different afterwards is the common shape. Resolve such a tension in the ticket: say which item
wins and what bounded deviation the other tolerates.

## The mechanics

- A dependency is recorded, never remembered: `--depends-on` when filing, `ticket depends <id> --add
  <ids>` on a filed ticket. Bare ids (`ticket depends 5 3`) replace the whole list.
- Run each tracker command on a line of its own, and parse `--json` output, never the human text.
- Never write a file under `.agent-progress-v2/` with a file tool, edit a ticket only below its
  frontmatter (`ticket show <id>` prints its path), and never commit the tracker.

## Closing

Tell the user, one line per ticket, its id, title, dependencies and epic, every ticket you merged or
abandoned and why, and the draft closed or left open with its id and open question numbers. Then stop.
